spec: Build a notification hub. Services publish events to a central SNS topic; subscribers register through a REST API choosing a channel (email-like or webhook-like), and each channel is backed by its own SQS queue subscribed to the topic. Subscriptions are stored in DynamoDB, and an endpoint reports how many messages each channel queue has received.

complexity.rationale: Topic-to-channel fan-out requires subscription management, routing, and delivery observation.

congruence_checklist: Per-channel SQS queues subscribed to the topic
Publish endpoint pushing events to the topic

plan.summary: A FastAPI notification hub that lets services publish events to a central SNS topic and lets consumers register subscriptions through a REST API. Each delivery channel (email-like or webhook-like) is backed by its own SQS queue that is subscribed to the SNS topic; subscription records are persisted in DynamoDB. A stats endpoint reports approximate message counts for each channel queue, and a drain/receive endpoint lets callers inspect queued notifications. Callers are internal microservices and operators using HTTP/JSON.

endpoints.purpose: Liveness check that also confirms connectivity to SNS, SQS and DynamoDB.
Register a subscriber: validate the channel (email|webhook), persist the subscription record in DynamoDB, and ensure the channel's SQS queue is subscribed to the SNS topic.
List subscriptions, optionally filtered by channel or endpoint.
Fetch a single subscription record by id.
Delete a subscription record from DynamoDB (marking it inactive/removed).
Publish an event to the central SNS topic with message attributes (event_type, channel) so it fans out to the channel queues.
List the supported channels and their backing SQS queue URLs/ARNs.
Receive (peek and optionally delete) messages from a channel's SQS queue for inspection or delivery simulation.
Report per-channel queue metrics: approximate number of messages received/available, in flight, and subscription counts.

data_models.name: Subscription
fields: target: str (email address or webhook URL)

data_models.name: EventPublishRequest
fields: channel: str | None (target a single channel; default fan-out to all)

aws_resources.name: notification-hub-events
aws_resources.justification: Central topic that services publish events to via POST /events; fans out to the per-channel queues.

aws_resources.name: notification-hub-email-queue
aws_resources.justification: Backing queue for the email-like channel, subscribed to the SNS topic; read by GET /channels/email/messages and measured by GET /stats.

aws_resources.name: notification-hub-webhook-queue
aws_resources.justification: Backing queue for the webhook-like channel, subscribed to the SNS topic; read by GET /channels/webhook/messages and measured by GET /stats.

aws_resources.name: notification-hub-dlq
aws_resources.justification: Dead-letter queue attached via redrive policy to both channel queues so undeliverable notifications are retained rather than lost.

aws_resources.name: notification-hub-email-subscription
aws_resources.justification: SNS-to-SQS subscription (raw message delivery) wiring the email channel queue to the central topic so publishes reach that channel.

aws_resources.name: notification-hub-webhook-subscription
aws_resources.justification: SNS-to-SQS subscription (raw message delivery) wiring the webhook channel queue to the central topic.

aws_resources.name: notification-hub-subscriptions
aws_resources.justification: Stores Subscription records created/read/deleted by the /subscriptions endpoints; partition key subscription_id with a GSI on channel for channel-filtered listing and counts.

aws_resources.name: notification-hub-app-policy
aws_resources.justification: Least-privilege policy/role for the backend service granting sns:Publish/ListSubscriptionsByTopic, sqs:ReceiveMessage/DeleteMessage/GetQueueAttributes, and dynamodb:PutItem/GetItem/Query/Scan/DeleteItem on the planned resources.

aws_resources.name: notification-hub-queue-policies
aws_resources.justification: SQS queue policies allowing the SNS topic principal to send messages to each channel queue (required for the topic-to-queue fan-out).

aws_resources.name: notification-hub-logs
aws_resources.justification: Log group for application-emitted publish/subscription events so operators can trace notification flow.

assumptions: Exactly two fixed channels are supported — 'email' and 'webhook' — each with a pre-provisioned SQS queue created by Terraform; the API validates against this set rather than creating queues at runtime.
'Email-like' and 'webhook-like' mean the delivery semantics are simulated through SQS queues; no real SES email or outbound HTTP delivery is performed.

'How many messages each channel queue has received' is served from the SQS ApproximateNumberOfMessages / ApproximateNumberOfMessagesReceived-style queue attributes rather than a separately maintained counter.

The backend runs as a standalone FastAPI service started by the harness and calls SNS/SQS/DynamoDB directly, so no Lambda consumer or API Gateway front door is planned; message consumption happens on-demand via the /channels/{channel}/messages endpoint.
Subscription ids are server-generated UUID4 strings; duplicate (channel, target) pairs are allowed but return the existing-style record semantics of a new id.
SNS subscriptions use raw message delivery so message bodies are the published JSON payload plus hub metadata.
No authentication is specified; endpoints are unauthenticated and assumed to run inside a trusted network, and no Secrets Manager secret is required.
Region defaults to us-east-1 and all endpoints are reachable through the LocalStack edge endpoint configured via AWS_ENDPOINT_URL.
